title: CCPA imposes ₹1 lakh fine on Britannia over '100% whole wheat bread' claim
description:
The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed a penalty of Rs 1 lakh on Britannia Industries Ltd for a misleading advertisement that claimed "100% whole wheat bread" even though the product's declared wheat content is just 62 per cent.
In its order dated October 22, the CCPA, headed by Chief Commissioner Nidhi Khare, directed the company to discontinue the advertisement with immediate effect across all print and electronic media, including social media.
Britannia has also been asked to submit a compliance report within 15 days.
The regulator took suo motu cognisance of the matter after noticing that the packaging of the product declared a wheat content of 62 per cent, despite the "100%" claim in its advertisements.
"In the present matter, the product admittedly contains only 62% whole wheat, while the remaining 38% comprises other ingredients, including rice bran and other constituents," the order said.
It added that the claim, prefixed with "100%", was prima facie
